chunks: Aban, from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The armor of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), known as Dhat al-Fudul, had two rings of silver in its front and two rings of silver in its back.' And he said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) wore it on the Day of al-Jamal.'

key_terms.ذَاتُ الْفُضُولِ: Dhat al-Fudul (Name of the armor, literally 'The One of Excellence/Abundance')
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجَمَلِ: The Day of the Camel (Battle of the Camel)

ai.seo_question: What were the distinctive features of the Prophet's armor and who wore it during the Battle of the Camel?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the specific design of the Prophet’s armor, known as *Dhat al-Fudul*, featuring silver rings on its front and back, which highlights the material continuity between the Prophet and his successor. It explicitly links this relic to Imam Ali’s (AS) leadership during the Battle of the Camel, underscoring the Shia view of his legitimate authority and the transmission of prophetic heritage through the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali: H 14959 – Aban, from Yahya Bin Abu Al-A’la who said:

I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The armour of the Rasool Allahsaww, Zat Al-Fuzoul had two rings of foil in front of it, and two rings of foil at the back of it’. And said; ‘Aliasws wore it on the Day of Al-Jamal’.
en.sarwar: 512. Aban, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb, who has said:

Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said: ‘Ali (a.s.) tightened a glimmering belt around his (a.s.) abdomen on the Day of Al-Jamal which Jibraeel (as) had descended with from the sky, and the Rasool Allah (saww) used to wear it around his (saww) abdomen whenever he (saww) wore the armour’.
